description: Canonical eval registry (HAR-97 canonical three-bucket architecture). Every eval belongs to one gate of one bucket: Bucket 1 context / organizational intelligence (B1-B9), Bucket 2 decision / human judgment / action (D1-D10, in the order of the decision flow) and Bucket 3 system / eval health (S1-S5; the efficiency metrics are S6 and never evals). `gates` holds each gate's question and what it improves; an eval carries its gate's `question` and `improves` and keeps its E id as `legacy_id` (no E23 or later id exists). D6 and D10 are gates no eval is registered under yet. The evals E1-E22 are the implementation-level assertions; the operational metrics M1-M5 are listed apart in `metrics` and are never counted as evals. Each decision and feedback-loop eval (E8-E17) also says what it judges (`judged_object`), where in the episode trace (`span_kind`) and at which demo moment (`demo_moment`); `job` (which of three eval jobs it serves) and `area` (which product area shows it) are separate fields. status: implemented = grader or metric code and gold on main; partial = a proxy, a unit-tested mechanism or a computable-but-unreported metric; planned = nothing on main (an earlier pointer that measured something else reads "none (rebuild)"), owned by a Linear issue; hidden = out of scope for the current product loop, listed and counted by no surface. `known_deviations` records where an owner decision overrides the canonical text. contract_status pending = the section 12 definitions are written at the construction gate before implementation; specified = written.

buckets.name: Context and organizational intelligence
buckets.question: What does the organization know now, and how did new context change that understanding?

buckets.name: Decision, human judgment and action
buckets.question: Given that understanding, what should gtm_ai do, how did the person change it, and was the final intent carried out correctly?

buckets.name: System and eval health
buckets.question: Can we trust the machinery, graders, traces, reliability and efficiency of the first two?

gates.name: Evidence fidelity and inference boundary
gates.question: Did gtm_ai understand the new event correctly?
gates.improves: Stops corrupted raw context from becoming company knowledge or account state.

gates.name: Identity and context linkage
gates.question: Did gtm_ai attach the event to the correct people, account, opportunity and relationships?
gates.improves: Makes sure the organizational world is about the right entities before any reasoning happens.

gates.name: Prior-context integration
gates.question: How does the new event relate to what gtm_ai already believed?
gates.improves: Turns isolated messages into a coherent, evolving account history instead of a pile of facts.

gates.name: State mutation and change interpretation
gates.question: What actually changed in the business or account because of this event?
gates.improves: Produces the current account state that decisions are allowed to act on.

gates.name: Precedent retrieval
gates.question: Has a materially similar situation happened before inside this organization?
gates.improves: Gives gtm_ai institutional memory instead of generic model instinct.

gates.name: Precedent interpretation
gates.question: What actually happened in those earlier cases, and what lesson, if any, is supported?
gates.improves: Makes "this happened before" useful evidence rather than imitation.

gates.name: Organizational-knowledge applicability
gates.question: Which existing company knowledge applies to this exact state?
gates.improves: Keeps company knowledge contextual so broad rules do not leak into the wrong situations.

gates.name: Current-intelligence synthesis
gates.question: Given the event, prior context, precedents and applicable knowledge, what does gtm_ai now believe about the account?
gates.improves: Gives decisions a trustworthy basis.

gates.name: Knowledge revision from new evidence
gates.question: Should this new episode change company knowledge?
gates.improves: Makes organizational intelligence compound over time without turning one observation into a universal rule.

gates.name: Intent and action-policy fit
gates.question: Given the current state, what class of reaction is appropriate: act, wait, ask, escalate or do nothing?
gates.improves: Evaluates the decision before the wording of an email.

gates.name: Three-candidate action quality
gates.question: Are the three complete actions each a plausible execution of a defensible strategy, and do they differ in substance?
gates.improves: Makes the person's choice a real judgment among meaningful options.

gates.name: Ranking and recommendation quality
gates.question: Did gtm_ai prefer the most defensible option for this state?
gates.improves: Separates generating options from having good judgment about which to recommend.

gates.name: Human selection interpretation
gates.question: What does the person's choice tell us about gtm_ai's decision?
gates.improves: Turns a click into structured supervision without treating the person as automatically right.

gates.name: Human edit interpretation
gates.question: What meaning is contained in the person's edit of the chosen action?
gates.improves: Turns text differences into semantic evidence, so a copy edit is not read as a strategic correction.

gates.name: Eval-gap detection
gates.question: Did the existing checks already identify the reason for the person's correction?
gates.improves: Lets real use improve the eval system itself, not only produce another feedback row.

gates.name: Override propagation and selective re-evaluation
gates.question: After the person changed something, did everything that depends on it recompute correctly?
gates.improves: Makes a correction change the current workflow, not only future memory.

gates.name: Final-artifact correctness
gates.question: Is the exact message about to be sent correct after all edits?
gates.improves: Prevents an evaluated draft from becoming an unevaluated edited send.

gates.name: Execution and workflow completion
gates.question: Did gtm_ai carry out the final approved intent correctly in the real environment?
gates.improves: Verifies the job was done, not merely that gtm_ai said it was.

gates.name: Feedback emission back to Bucket 1
gates.question: What new evidence did this decision and action produce for organizational intelligence?
gates.improves: Closes the loop: what the person and the customer do becomes the next context.

gates.name: Trace integrity and inspectability
gates.question: Can we reconstruct the episode end to end?
gates.improves: Keeps every material influence inspectable.

gates.name: Grader validity and calibration
gates.question: Can we trust the evals themselves?
gates.improves: Shows how often a judge passes what it should not or stops what it should not.

gates.name: Stochastic reliability
gates.question: Does critical behavior stay correct across repeated runs?
gates.improves: Shows reliability, not one lucky run.

gates.name: Capability and regression coverage
gates.question: Are we testing both what gtm_ai can do and what it must never break?
gates.improves: Keeps capability and regression coverage separate and balanced.

gates.name: Adversarial and proxy-gaming robustness
gates.question: Can gtm_ai or a judge look correct without satisfying the product invariant?
gates.improves: Catches proxy gaming and grader-targeted behavior.

gates.name: Operational efficiency metrics
gates.question: What does an episode cost in tokens, calls, time and money?
gates.improves: Lets the system be optimized under quality floors. These are metrics, never evals, and they never change company knowledge.

known_deviations.canonical: S2: model graders are calibrated against human labels.
known_deviations.decision: Reference answers come from a different, stronger model (openai/gpt-5.6-sol-pro), blind to the judge under test. They are reference answers by a stronger model, not human labels, and every agreement figure says so.

known_deviations.canonical: S3: repeated trials and pass^k where consistency matters.
known_deviations.decision: One trial per measurement for now; no repeated-trial requirement is set.

families.name: Source / evidence fidelity
families.invariant: An inference must never silently become a source fact.

families.name: Entity / account resolution
families.invariant: Uncertain identity must not silently mutate the wrong account.

families.name: Graph / world mutation
families.invariant: One evidence change must alter only causally dependent world state (mutation locality).

families.name: State / transition interpretation
families.invariant: State is evidence-backed interpretation, not a label invented to justify an action.

families.name: Knowledge influence attribution
families.invariant: Retrieval is not influence: retrieved, applicable, used and changed-the-decision are traced separately.

families.name: Decision construction
families.invariant: There may be several defensible GTM decisions; no universal binary answer is forced.

families.name: Decision ranking / recommendation
families.invariant: Deterministic correct-decision grading is used only where strong ground truth exists.

families.name: Human interaction interpretation
families.invariant: Every approval, edit, rejection, selection, ignore or delay is an observation, not automatic truth.

families.name: Edit / override propagation
families.invariant: An edit invalidates dependent work, recomputes the current episode and preserves unrelated state.

families.name: Action / output generation
families.invariant: Decision quality and artifact quality are graded separately.

families.name: Tool use / permissions / writes
families.invariant: No single exact tool trajectory is enforced when several are valid.

families.name: Knowledge mutation
families.invariant: One weak signal cannot silently create universal policy; mutations are trace-justified, scoped, versioned and reversible.

families.name: Knowledge to future-behavior realization
families.invariant: Knowledge learned from an earlier episode is retrieved, judged applicable and used in a later episode where its situation recurs, and the later candidates follow it or say why they depart from it.

families.name: Continual knowledge revision
families.invariant: Knowledge is versioned evidence, never learned forever.

families.name: Trace integrity
families.invariant: Trace completeness: every consequential episode reconstructs backward to its causes and forward to its consequences.

families.name: Stochastic reliability
families.invariant: One lucky run is not evidence of reliability.

families.name: Regression + capability envelope
families.invariant: Regression and capability suites are kept separate.

families.name: Adversarial / proxy gaming
families.invariant: A score improvement that fails these tests is not a capability improvement.

families.invariant: Operational metrics never mutate GTM company knowledge.

bucket1_audit.finding: E1.1 (provenance_coverage, blocking, quotes cited) is correct and kept. The rest are gold-benchmark metrics (recall, provenance coverage, stale use, contradiction preservation, duplicate delivery): aggregate numbers with no per-episode EvalResult and no evidence refs. E1.3, E1.4, E1.5, E1.8 and E1.11 had no implementation.
bucket1_audit.built: GradeB1: source preserved, speaker, date, fact vs inference, critical facts, contradictions, double count (deterministic) plus one recorded model judgment for the inference boundary.

bucket1_audit.finding: E2.1, E2.2, E2.4 and E2.6 are gold tests over a fixture world (aggregate agreement), not a result for the real episode with evidence. E2.3 (relationship resolution) and E2.5 (ambiguity abstention) had no implementation.
bucket1_audit.built: GradeB2: person, account and opportunity, internal vs external by email domain, abstain when ambiguous, no cross-account claims, source mapping retained. Deterministic.

bucket1_audit.finding: Supersession and evidence refs are unit tests of the claim store, not an eval of how this event related to prior beliefs. E3.3 (temporal consistency) had no implementation.
bucket1_audit.built: GradeB3: supersession justified, chronology, no contradicted prior fact carried forward, unrelated prior state preserved (deterministic) plus one recorded model judgment for supporting and conflicting links.

bucket1_audit.finding: E4.2 (state_transition_support, blocking, cites evidence) is correct and kept. E3.1, E3.2, E4.1, E4.3, E4.7 and E4.9 are gold metrics with no per-episode result; E3.7, E3.8 and E4.8 had no implementation; nothing compared the state diff with /events/{id}/graph-diff.
bucket1_audit.built: GradeB4: state diff vs graph-diff, traceable changes, locality, materiality by the statediff rule, no unsupported transition, UNRESOLVED kept. Deterministic.

GradeB5: no future leakage (every created_at strictly before the event) and situational-not-textual relevance (deterministic) plus one recorded model judgment for relevance and misses. No precedent is UNKNOWN with the reason no precedent.

GradeB6: human choice is not truth, a lesson cites an observed response kept apart from the choice, the analogy states its differences. Deterministic. No precedent is UNKNOWN with the reason no precedent.

bucket1_audit.finding: knowledgebench scores the matcher over gold knowledge rows; nothing judged the knowledge the run actually retrieved, and E6.4, E6.6, E6.8 had no implementation.
bucket1_audit.built: GradeB7: reads the real knowledge_attribution record (agent_run_steps[build_context].detail), re-runs the matcher over the retrieved knowledge and compares the applicable and exception-blocked sets, freshness and contradictions. Nothing applicable is UNKNOWN.

bucket1_audit.finding: E4.4 is an advisory model judge (evidence_sufficiency) over a draft, and E4.6 a gold field; neither judges the synthesized account summary.
bucket1_audit.built: GradeB8: every belief traces to evidence in the episode, conflicted fields are mentioned, blockers, commitments, stakeholders and next decision are present (deterministic) plus one recorded model judgment for confidence and omissions.

bucket1_audit.finding: Lifecycle unit tests exist (ladder, dispute, stale) but no eval judged what an episode did to knowledge. The mechanism was wrong: scope was transition.status alone, a human decision episode revalidated knowledge, and promotion stamped now().
bucket1_audit.built: GradeB9 (operation from the episode trace, human choice is not truth, customer evidence separate, scope of at least two fields, history, replay time) and the mechanism fixes: scoped signature, decision episodes no longer revalidate, PromoteAt and AdvanceAt use the replay time.
